title: [17/8/2024] The production of three forest industry products

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the production volume of three forest industry products, namely timber, pulp, and paper, measured in million tonnes, in a European country between 1980 and 1996.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, despite some fluctuations, all three products showed an upward trend in production over the twenty-year period. In addition, paper manufacturing experienced the most significant growth, ending the period as the highest-volume product.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at pulp production first, it started at approximately 4.5 million tonnes in 1980 and rose steadily to reach its peak of about 9.5 million tonnes in 1984. However, after this point, the figures began to decline gradually, falling to about 7.5 million tonnes by the end of the period, despite some minor fluctuations between 1990 and 1996.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the other two products, in 1980, timber production began at a higher level of approximately 5.5 million tonnes, while paper output started at the lowest point among all three products, at around 3.8 million tonnes. Paper production then showed the most dramatic increase, rising consistently throughout the period to reach 12 million tonnes in 1996, making it the most-produced item. A similar but less pronounced upward trend was seen in timber output, though it first experienced a sharp drop to about 3 million tonnes in 1982, before recovering and growing steadily to end the period at approximately 9.5 million tonnes.
